subject.title: Feature: Respect userTimezone in memory file timestamps and naming

question: Should bundled session-memory filenames and `# Session` headers follow `agents.defaults.userTimezone` when it differs from the gateway host timezone?
rationale: Current docs and shipped code define session-memory as host-local, while memory-core auto-flush already follows configured user timezone; changing the hook affects persisted artifact naming semantics and needs an owner decision.

options.title: Adopt `userTimezone` for session-memory
options.body: Treat session-memory artifacts as part of the existing user-timezone contract, reuse the shared timezone helpers, and update tests/docs for the new semantics.

options.title: Keep host-local session-memory
options.body: Leave session-memory aligned with the gateway host local date and close or narrow this request to auto-flush behavior, which is already configured-timezone aware.

options.title: Add a separate memory timezone knob
options.body: Introduce a dedicated memory artifact timezone only if maintainers want a distinct contract and are willing to own schema/docs/doctor migration work.

recommendation.title: Adopt `userTimezone` for session-memory
recommendation.body: Treat session-memory artifacts as part of the existing user-timezone contract, reuse the shared timezone helpers, and update tests/docs for the new semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the current host-local session-memory behavior and related docs/tests, making them the closest current-history owner for the decision.
